correctness.rationale: The domain is the bi-infinite two-row ladder, with only finite occupied connected components constrained to odd sizes. At most one component meets a vertical cut, so its parity and the 4 possible masks form a complete 7-state automaton. The rule is derived by checking mask overlap and odd closure. Zero-bounded words have exactly a_n=(M^(n+1))_ZZ. Row symmetry gives the stated five-state B; exact symbolic computation verifies its characteristic polynomial and rational resolvent. B^2 is positive, yielding Perron exponential growth. Every legal n-word admits correction of boundary components with at most one extra column on each side; hence a_n<=L_n<=a_(n+2), proving the entropy. Exhaustive independent graph-component enumeration matches n=0..8, and exact polynomial identities are checked by executable code; tests are not the proof.

value.rationale: The odd-component subshift is a concrete geometric constraint used to separate one- and higher-dimensional sofic phenomena. Its first nontrivial transverse restriction (two rows) has a natural yet previously unreported numerical entropy and complete finite-board connected-component parity census. The exact algebraic root and rational generating series quantify the effect of allowing vertical connectivity; they are reusable finite-width benchmarks and establish a scale beyond the one-row odd-run language without pretending to solve planar entropy. This is a complete natural exact invariant, not an arbitrary parameter slice.
